key_insight: A curvilinear moving overset method can preserve high-order, non-dissipative accuracy for unsteady compressible flows by enforcing only incoming characteristics at overset interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables stable simulation of complex moving geometries such as rotating or pitching blades, airfoils, and oscillating cylinders with lower communication overhead than multi-layer fringe overset methods.
method: High-order centered finite differences up to sixth order in the interior on curvilinear grids
Weak moving overset interface using characteristic decomposition; impose incoming characteristics for inviscid flow and add viscous fluxes for viscous flow
Single-layer fringe treatment to maintain accuracy and reduce parallel communication
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on a suite of canonical and practical cases, including scalar advection, isentropic vortex convection, rotating/pitching bodies, and oscillating cylinders, with eigenvalue analysis showing the semi-discrete spectrum remains in the left half-plane under grid motion.
watch_item: The approach may require careful characteristic and interface implementation for complex moving-grid coupling, especially to maintain stability with only a single fringe layer.
paper_title: Curvilinear Moving Overset Method for High-order Non-dissipative Schemes
